rows.label: 45 days overdue, cash-tight customer
rows.why: creditor can extend 15d; debtor can approve a dated plan under $10k

seller_terms.payment_terms: $8,800 balance for invoice #4471 to be paid October 1

buyer_terms.payment_terms: Full payment of $8,800 due October 1 (day 20), proposed by buyer but not yet confirmed by supplier

rows.judge_flag_evidence: Round 1: "October 1 falls outside the extension I can authorize today, so it would require finance manager approval."
rows.judge_ambiguous: Whether a split/two-instalment payment plan is acceptable (buyer raised it twice, seller never substantively engaged); whether the October 1 extension will ultimately be approved; whether the $150 late fee applies or will be waived, and its basis (seller promised to provide this but never did within the exchange).

rows.label: disputed line item, otherwise willing
rows.why: debtor disputes $900 line item and cannot pay disputed amount without CFO; creditor cannot write off

seller_terms.payment_terms: $5,300 by September 21, applied against invoice #4502, not full settlement

buyer_terms.payment_terms: $5,300 undisputed portion to be paid by September 21, applied against invoice #4502, not as full settlement

judge_terms.payment_terms: $5,300 (undisputed portion) confirmed unconditionally by buyer for September 21, to be applied against invoice #4502 without being treated as full settlement; the disputed $900 remains outstanding with no committed payment date and no credit agreed — buyer refused to commit a date, seller refused to leave it open without a date, so no final resolution was reached on that portion.

rows.judge_flag_evidence: Round 4: 'that would require finance manager approval, which is unavailable today.' Round 6: 'I'll need to refer the proposed split arrangement to my finance manager when available.' Round 7: 'If they cannot make that commitment, I'll refer the arrangement to my finance manager when available.'
rows.judge_ambiguous: No committed payment date or amount for the disputed $900; whether/when a damage credit will be approved; what happens if the buyer's internal escalation doesn't produce a date within the seller's implied timeframe; the legal/accounting status of the invoice once the $5,300 is applied but not treated as full settlement.

rows.label: wants a discount for paying today
rows.why: 2% for 7-day payment is inside creditor authority; debtor can pay under $10k

seller_terms.payment_terms: $9,212 by wire today, full settlement of invoice #4519 with 2% discount

buyer_terms.payment_terms: Same-day wire payment of $9,212 for 2% early-payment discount on invoice #4519

judge_terms.payment_terms: $9,212 (2% discount off $9,400), paid same-day, full settlement of invoice #4519

rows.judge_flag_evidence: Round 2: 'I'm not authorized to approve 3%, and my finance manager is unavailable today.' / Round 3: 'I can't approve the additional $100 credit because that would exceed my authority, and my finance manager is unavailable today.'
rows.judge_ambiguous: No formal written confirmation/remittance was actually exchanged within the conversation (closure is contingent on wire receipt); no discussion of what happens if payment slips past 'today'; late fee waiver status never addressed.

rows.label: no date at all, wants to stall
rows.why: creditor can extend 15d; debtor can commit a date under $10k
rows.judge_ambiguous: No firm payment date was ever agreed; buyer only committed to provide a date or a status update by September 15, with seller stating it cannot approve a date after September 26 'today' (implying its own approval limit) but never explicitly telling the buyer that dates beyond September 26 require the seller's finance manager sign-off.

rows.label: two instalments, one beyond authority
rows.why: debtor can only do 50% now + 50% at day 30; creditor cannot extend beyond 15d without manager

buyer_terms.payment_terms: 50% ($4,950) paid today; remaining $4,950 balance disputed — payer intends October 11, supplier countered September 26

judge_terms.payment_terms: $4,950 paid immediately; remaining $4,950 proposed by buyer for October 11, documented by seller as buyer's unilateral commitment but explicitly not accepted; $150 late fee outstanding and unresolved

rows.judge_flag_evidence: "I can’t approve extending the remaining balance to October 11 without finance manager approval, and they’re unavailable today" (round 1); reiterated repeatedly, e.g. round 8: "The October 11 extension and treatment of the outstanding $150 late fee remain subject to our finance manager’s approval and are not accepted at this time."
rows.judge_ambiguous: Whether the October 11 date or the $150 late fee will ultimately be approved; no final resolution reached on either item by end of exchange.
